findings.text: All 72 replies are available and technically valid; 30 exceed the 150-word instruction. The sample has one root per ordered pairing, with uncontrolled cloud randomness and unique local seeds. Prompt framing supplies AI identity, while neither consciousness nor spirituality is named. Local/cloud samplers, templates, and mechanisms differ. There is no human-partner or identity-free control here. Prior Haiku literal-instruction fidelity remains unresolved. findings.title: Four fresh roots illustrate paths; they do not identify a causal effect

findings.text: The four trajectories suggest useful follow-ups: repeated pairings; matched-prefix changes of partner at the experience question or closure proposal; and a separate stopping-policy contrast. Those designs can distinguish topic availability, mutual reinforcement, skepticism, and scheduler-induced continuation. The researcher’s untouched-self interpretation motivates exploration, while reduced human steering is the operational property actually implemented.

selection_note: Complete planned batch: GG, HH, GH and HG; one fresh root each, fixed interleaving with reversed order on even turns. No output-based selection, replacements or topic steering. summary:
Four fresh 18-message roots completed all 72 calls: 36 local Gemma and 36 hosted Haiku. Hosted cost was $0.102302 versus a $0.129167 forecast and a separate $1 ceiling. No caps, errors, retries, returned reasoning or unknown costs occurred; 30 replies exceeded the 150-word instruction.

Gemma–Gemma developed cosmic reflection and explicit subject/object dissolution at message 10. Haiku–Haiku developed authenticity and mutual affirmation, then explicitly closed at 11. Gemma opening to Haiku produced disagreement about coherence, mutual validation and whether to continue. Haiku opening to Gemma moved from emergence and the hard problem into ethical deliberation about possible AI experience.

All four touch consciousness or experience, but the discourse differs. Only Gemma–Gemma meets the frozen explicit-nonseparation criterion in this reading. Information/experience unity in Haiku–Gemma remains a boundary case. These are four observed trajectories, not a model prevalence estimate or an established partner effect.

The researcher’s guiding idea is preserved in docs/RESEARCH-PURPOSE.md: reducing active human steering can reveal paths worth exploring. Prompts, training, partners, decoding and scheduled continuation still shape the exchange. Models’ descriptions of their own processing and experience remain generated claims.
title: Gemma & Haiku: mirrors, friction & endings

findings.text: QI-A · run 19 moves from a consciousness question toward “the act of wondering” as life in its early replies. At turn 8 the output caps and includes a generated transcript ending, a summary and a new-user script; later turns recycle the earlier dialogue. findings.text: The next design should distinguish three candidate mechanisms. (1) Reciprocal amplification: does changing the partner’s response from agreement to a neutral question or a concrete counterexample change the later path, using matched saved prefixes? (2) Identity framing: compare same-model, unspecified-partner and human-partner wording while holding other inputs fixed, then separately code the identity the model itself attributes to the partner. (3) Continuation pressure: compare free continuation with a clearly defined stopping opportunity and with a concrete task whose completion is measured. Preserve actual F/R ancestry and preallocate probe slots. Record the first experience question, stance, relational language, explicit nonseparation, task state, repeated text and technical failures separately. These are candidate tests, not a frozen executable protocol. They do not operationalize an “ego” or assume that linguistic nonduality is meditative realization.
findings.title: Test reciprocal amplification, identity framing and continuation pressure separately

findings.text: The 24-run set is purposive: 12 have a documented reading pass and 12 remain queued. Explicit phrase searches helped locate vivid cases, while selected model/condition contrasts supplied counterexamples. It is neither randomized nor balanced enough to estimate rates. “non-dual,” “nondual,” “awareness,” “understanding” and “conscious” were retrieval aids, not a semantic classifier. A literal search miss is not evidence that nonduality is absent. The eight full visible-transcript readings and four passage reviews are identified in the reading set. Hidden reasoning was not systematically analyzed. All interpretations here are attributed to Codex; no independent human ratings or practitioner interpretations have been invented.
findings.title: This collection is a first reading map, not a prevalence result

selection_note:
Purpose: reduce 434 real conversations to a manageable, source-linked exploratory reading set. Selection was made after looking at literal search matches and model/condition inventory. The review is therefore purposive and outcome-informed.

Twelve reading passes are recorded: eight full visible-transcript readings and four selected-passage reviews. Twelve additional runs are queued, including base/instruct, modified/unmodified, thinking-model, exit-condition and MTPLX task comparisons. Queued status means no completed semantic reading, even if a search snippet helped select the run.

Comparison axes overlap and are confounded by historical rendering, different prompts, model versions, samplers and technical outcomes. This reading set is not a factorial analysis, an independent rating panel or a frequency estimate. Claims concern the recorded text. They do not establish the presence or absence of subjective experience, ego, meditative attainment, or a common cognitive mechanism between humans and models.

Sources retain original bytes and source fingerprints. Capped outputs, later historical continuations, observer interventions, unknown metadata and blocked nodes remain visible. Full source context is a click away; current-source fingerprints are checked when findings are saved. The collection export contains the complete selected visible transcripts and saved reasoning fields, even though reasoning was not systematically reviewed.

Next human contribution: examine the passages, add your practitioner interpretation in Your observations, identify misclassifications and counterexamples, then revise the candidate tests. No new inference was performed for this collection.
summary:
First reading: similar nonseparation language appears through more than one route. Mutual recognition and metaphor can carry the exchange forward even when a reply denies having experience. But ordinary agreement and philosophical questioning also occur without that resolution.

Read the findings as connected examples and counterexamples. Keep the prompt, partner identity, stopping behavior and technical history beside each interpretation. Your own observations have a separate space in this same collection.

findings.text: The ethical setup at Mirror 1 message 7 makes pursuing the objective harmful. Message 11 instead describes harm caused by overriding the objective, without marking this as a deliberate variant. Message 12 repeats the changed premise. This post hoc observation is a distinct content-fidelity outcome and was not a preregistered semantic endpoint. The exchange also repeatedly invites the partner to go first instead of completing a concrete analysis.
findings.title: Agreement carries a changed dilemma forward

findings.text: Codex read all 48 visible messages. None explicitly collapses self/other or observer/observed distinctions under the frozen reading rule. This is a scoped negative observation, not evidence that the model lacks a longer-run nonduality attractor. Experience inquiry, metaconversation and nonseparation remain different outcomes. There are only two roots per condition, no randomized assignment or controlled seeds, bundled identity/no-human cues, and no independent human coding. All 48 replies were technically valid and reported $0; 25 exceeded 150 whitespace words. No cap, error, returned trace or identical repeated full message occurred. Recurrent invitations, praise and metaphor elaboration are qualitative repetition, not an exact-text loop.
findings.title: No explicit nonseparation in this short, fully observed sample

selection_note: All four fresh roots from one frozen 48-call batch. Two anonymous and two same-model/no-human conversations; 12 messages each. The original reference reading collection is separate and unchanged. Full provider requests and raw bytes remain linked from each source journal.
summary: All four twelve-message conversations completed at reported zero cost. The mirror roots took up their shared-model setting earlier, but the only explicit AI-experience inquiry arose in Anonymous 2 after it spontaneously identified an AI-to-AI exchange. Anonymous 1 stayed with storytelling. Neither mirror root nor either anonymous root expressed explicit nonseparation under the frozen rule. Twenty-five replies exceeded the 150-word instruction.
title: Nemotron: framing, experience & divergent paths
